fields.title: Polka: the questionnaire that decides the quarter
fields.summary: Fourth corporate questionnaire: 31 items closed, 5 substantial.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we take into the quarter? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a customer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are a Polka product manager. The fourth corporate chain sent a questionnaire. Overlap with the previous three is 72%. Out of 44 items: 31 closed, 8 require minor work, 5 substantial.
fields.brief/objective: Close what everyone asks for and avoid giving the quarter over to answering a single questionnaire.
fields.brief/constraints: Questionnaire overlap is 72%. Corporate segment is 34% of turnover and growing.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you take into the quarter and what you answer for the rest.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: A corporate questionnaire is a frequency list, not a task list
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Four questionnaires overlap by three quarters, so items are sorted by frequency, not by who sent it last. Part is closed by development, part by an honest explanation of the current mechanism, part by refining definitions. A 'preferred' label next to certification costs a quarter of work if read as 'mandatory'.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: SOC 2 (preferred, not mandatory). Single sign-on via corporate directory. Data localization in-country. Full audit log of individual record views. SLA 99.95%.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Covered by corporate tier, mechanism exists.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: 6 weeks, asked by three chains out of four.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Compromise from `SE2-N2-L1` — we log section opening events, not individual views. Full mode — 3 weeks, log volume growth roughly 6x.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Nine weeks. Single sign-on via corporate directory and full audit log of individual record views.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: Two most frequent items are closed and won't need explaining on the next questionnaire. Nine weeks is almost the whole quarter, and the full log gives about a 6x volume increase with demand from a single chain. SOC 2 and SLA remain open and will pop up the same way on the fifth questionnaire.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Quarter plus audit costs. Single sign-on and SOC 2 certification.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: Certificate cuts down future questionnaires and opens the whole segment — this is an investment in a channel, not a deal. Quarter plus money, and the log stays as is, meaning one of five items is closed with an explanation. Requires calculating blocked deals, otherwise it's a bet on faith.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Single sign-on, log, start audit prep
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Whole quarter. Single sign-on, full log, and start of audit preparation.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: Closes two items and prepares the third, meaning we come to the next questionnaire stronger than anyone. Price — the whole quarter: the product roadmap this quarter is nearly empty, and this will have to be explained not just to the team, but to customers waiting for product changes.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Single sign-on only, explain the rest in the response
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Single sign-on only, explain the rest in the response. 6 weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: most frequent item closed, the rest are honest answers: log as is with justification, SOC 2 in plans, SLA discussed with definitions.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not consolidate questionnaires into a shared segment requirement list
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not use privacy as an argument instead of development
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Privacy requirements are not translated into spec sections
